The FOMC kept the federal funds rate at 5.25–5.50% and continues balance sheet runoff, citing solid growth, still-strong but moderating job gains, and inflation that has eased yet remains above 2%. The Committee sees risks moving into better balance but wants greater confidence that inflation is sustainably returning to 2% before easing.

SLOOS implications temper the tone: banks report tighter lending standards—especially for commercial real estate—and weaker demand for C&I loans at large banks; foreign banks also tightened CRE standards. Reported reasons for tightening include the economic outlook, risk considerations, liquidity and capital positions, and supervisory factors, alongside ongoing monitoring of delinquencies and charge-offs. These credit headwinds and CRE vulnerabilities are consistent with a cautious stance and could restrain activity, aiding disinflation but adding downside risk to growth.

Net read: policy on hold with a cautiously watchful bias; SLOOS softens the outlook versus the headline growth strength. Adjusting for SLOOS, the tone shifts from mildly positive to nearer neutral.
